scan_metadata.notes: Fresh shallow clone of the default branch (depth 20), so has_uncommitted_changes reflects the clone (false), not the author's working copy. Node is limited to a small VS Code extension (.vscode/niva, JavaScript LSP client); Shell scripts (install.sh, tests/integration/run.sh, fetch_testdata.sh) were skimmed only; full interface/data-access detection for shell is out of scope for skill version 1.0. Custom .niva flow files are a project DSL, not scanned as code. Binary/test data (gpkg, geojson, kmz, tif, png, pdf) excluded. This is a CLI/library/QGIS plugin, not a web service: no HTTP routes exist.

what_this_app_can_do: Runs geoprocessing pipelines written in a text grammar by translating them into QGIS Processing algorithm calls, reading and writing local geospatial files and database tables the user points it at.
Can send an ntfy push notification (default server ntfy.sh) and send SMTP email with an optional file attachment from the user's configured account.
Can write to databases through named QGIS connections, including server-side CREATE TABLE AS SELECT, when the user's flow requests it.
Can inventory a directory of geospatial datasets into a Markdown report and fetch layer listings from remote WFS/WMS/ArcGIS REST URLs.
Setup command can modify the user's PATH / shell rc files and download a marimo release from GitHub.

data_sources_touched.source: Local geospatial files (gpkg, shp, geojson, csv, rasters, point clouds)
Databases via named QGIS connections (PostGIS, SQLite/GeoPackage)
SMTP server (user-configured, Gmail default for Gmail senders)
Remote OGC/ArcGIS/XYZ services and GitHub downloads

capability_summary.who_can_reach_it: Local tool run by the user (CLI, QGIS plugin, LSP over stdio). No network listener or web routes were found, so it is reachable only by whoever runs it on their own machine.
unauthorized_action_red_flags: notify and email verbs can send data off the machine to ntfy.sh / an SMTP host chosen by the user; attachments can be any readable file path
sql verb executes arbitrary user-authored SQL, including writes, against configured database connections

top_findings: CI workflow contains a throwaway test-container Postgres password (.github/workflows/ci.yml:70), marked allowlist in detect-secrets
notify/email verbs can send data to external hosts (ntfy.sh, SMTP)
No web routes, no network listener; secrets resolved from env or QGIS encrypted auth store
